compression.title: Papers with Code
compression.lede: was a free, open-access platform linking machine learning papers to their code, data sets and benchmark results (Coursera), 2018–2025: a database whose benchmark tables were "the field's map of the state of the art" (MMRS record).

sentences.text: Papers with Code was a free, open-access platform that connected machine learning research papers to their code, data sets and benchmark results (Coursera; the Miraheze 'Learn AI' card opens with the same words), and the MMRS record defines it as a database (2018–2025) that linked machine learning papers to their code and reported results, its benchmark tables "the field's map of the state of the art", its unit the paper linked to its code, the tasks and datasets it reports on, and its results in benchmark tables (MMRS record).

TIB's blog calls it a community-driven platform for exploring and discovering state-of-the-art research in artificial intelligence and machine learning, which aggregated studies from multiple sources and served as a central hub for benchmarked research in the form of leaderboards (TIB-Blog); CodeSOTA calls it "in effect, the Wikipedia of machine-learning research": papers linked to implementations, benchmarks organised as <Task, Dataset, Metric> tuples, and leaderboards showing for each tuple who held the top score and with what code (CodeSOTA).

In its own words as TechCrunch reported them in 2020 it was "a free and open resource for machine learning papers and code", and the MMRS record reads its admission of items as not requiring harm (MMRS record).

The MMRS record records dead aggregators with the same fields as live ones, "the dead state, the date, and where the data went are part of the entity", and tests the composition layer's account of this one with a battery: founders and owner kept apart, the data dumps kept apart from the successors, CodeSOTA and Trending Papers not presented as Papers with Code, and no current result attributed to its tables (MMRS record).

Robert Stojnic and Ross Taylor debuted it in 2018 (Coursera) under Atlas ML, and Facebook became majority owner of the operating company, Deeptide Ltd., on 13 December 2019, the day Stojnic announced it was joining Facebook AI; TechCrunch, reporting the acquisition in February 2020, gave the price as about $40 million from its sources (MMRS record, whose operator field reads "Atlas ML (Deeptide Ltd.), majority-owned by Facebook from 13 December 2019 (later Meta)").

On joining Facebook AI in 2019 its users were reassured that it would "remain a neutral, open and free resource" (TIB-Blog, quoting the announcement); within a year it had grown into a resource of more than 18,000 papers and over 1,500 leaderboards (TIB-Blog), and at the merger it held over 18,000 papers, 1,500 leaderboards and over 1,000 tasks, Facebook operating it under Meta AI Research (Coursera).

It ran on an open contribution model, researchers submitting their own papers and linking them to code repositories without a central editorial team (Coursera), part of its data coming from the sources the sota-extractor lists (the paperswithcode-data README); it scaled because researchers could submit results from any model as reported in their papers, wherever the model was hosted (TIB-Blog), a paper-centric model (Coursera); how papers entered is among what the MMRS record has not checked (MMRS record).

Meta sunsetted it on 24–25 July 2025 without prior notice, users reporting "Bad Gateway 502" errors and garbled text and GitHub issues going unanswered (CodeSOTA, whose record gives its dates "as reported by the site's archived banner and community tracking"); Coursera dates the sunset 24 July 2025 (Coursera), and the MMRS record, which gives the same date, has read no notice from Meta itself (MMRS record).

Where its users were sent is held two ways in the field: "users were simply redirected to the Papers with Code Github repository" (TIB-Blog) and the domain was "now redirecting to GitHub" (a Reddit card of 6 August 2025), against "Within days, the domain began redirecting to Hugging Face's Trending Papers feature" (CodeSOTA) and "The platform now redirects to Hugging Face's Trending Papers section" (Coursera); paperswithcode.com today serves the page titled "Trending Papers - Hugging Face" (its own address), and the MMRS record reports the destination two ways and leaves the redirect target at the sunset unchecked (MMRS record).

The Capture Registry records that the two compositions of 29 October give the redirect two ways, one saying the site "initially redirected to Hugging Face Trending Papers", the other that it "redirected users to a static GitHub archive", and quotes the record as saying users were "pointed to Hugging Face" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29), a phrase the record's account of the destination, given two ways, does not contain (MMRS record).

About a month after it disappeared Hugging Face announced a successor platform in partnership with Papers with Code and Meta (TIB-Blog); Coursera has Julien Chaumond, Hugging Face's co-founder and CTO, announce a partnership with Meta to replace it the day after the sunset (Coursera), and the MMRS record has him announce the sunset the next day with Trending Papers, launched by Hugging Face with Meta, as its replacement, the site having failed with outages since early July (MMRS record, on hyper.ai's report); Coursera calls Hugging Face "the official successor to Papers With Code", replicating some of what it offered (Coursera).

Trending Papers carries no leaderboards (MMRS record); Hugging Face's leaderboards require the model to be publicly hosted on its Hub, which excludes many works that report results without deploying models that way (TIB-Blog); none of the successors Meta pointed at replicates "the unified paper-code-benchmark-dataset-method linkage" (CodeSOTA); "No single platform replicates everything Papers With Code offered" (Coursera); and the MMRS record holds that Papers with Code is not Hugging Face Trending Papers, its replacement (MMRS record).

TIB holds that benchmarks available only on commercial platforms "remain vulnerable to corporate decisions, shifting business models, or sudden shutdowns", public infrastructures such as the ORKG keeping them accessible (TIB-Blog); the MMRS record reads the entity as "A field aggregator held by a platform ended under that platform, and its record survives in dumps that others host" (MMRS record).

The archive places aggregators, as a class, among the means of semantic circulation (#1545), whose ownership is the semantic-bourgeois position (#1465; #1545); it distinguishes infrastructural means of circulation from procedural means of production "while recognizing that contemporary platforms frequently combine both" (#1545), lists aggregators beside platforms and employers as capturing the value of human semantic labour (#256), and asks of such ownership "whether that ownership is disclosed, whether it extracts from other producers, and whether its instruments remain usable by producers who do not own the infrastructure" (#1545).

Its data survives: the paperswithcode-data README offers "the full dataset behind" paperswithcode.com as five dumps and licenses all data under CC-BY-SA (the paperswithcode-data README), as the MMRS record restates (MMRS record) and Coursera confirms (Coursera); the ORKG imported its data in 2021, keeping benchmarks that would otherwise have been lost (TIB-Blog), and CodeSOTA counts the rescue as JSON dumps on GitHub, the pwc-archive on Hugging Face and the ORKG's imports: "The data survives; the integrated experience does not" (CodeSOTA).

The README still says "At the moment, data is regenerated daily" (the paperswithcode-data README), while Coursera reports the repository last updated on 8 September 2025 and both archives static, nothing added to the field since July 2025 appearing in either (Coursera); the MMRS record gives the cadence as ended July 2025, the dumps having been regenerated daily, its version history as final dumps only, and reads the dumps as preserving "its tables as of the end" (MMRS record).
TIB closes by asking those disappointed to see it discontinued to contribute their papers to the ORKG (TIB-Blog).

"Papers With Code was retired by Meta in July 2025", its old leaderboards are not maintained, and its 9,327 benchmark leaderboards, 79,817 paper-to-code linkages and 5,628 datasets are no longer served from the canonical URL, with CodeSOTA for live pages and the frozen archive for history; CodeSOTA holds that drift made its late-stage tables unreliable (CodeSOTA).

The MMRS record gives its count as CodeSOTA gives it and has not checked the counts against the dumps, states "its benchmark tables are NOT current state of the art", and holds that a current result attributed to paperswithcode.com comes from a table that stopped updating in July 2025 (MMRS record).

CodeSOTA presents itself as "the v2 replacement for what PWC did", with reproduced scores, verification dates, code links and lineage (CodeSOTA); the MMRS record records that CodeSOTA carries the name in its own paths and presents itself as a successor, and that Papers with Code is not CodeSOTA (MMRS record).

Its name now has a live instance, a revival at paperswithcode.co, which the MMRS record keeps as a separate entity: paperswithcode.com is not live since 24 July 2025, the revival is not paperswithcode.com, and the original's frozen dumps, CodeSOTA's succession claim and the revival are "three entities around one name" (MMRS record).

Niels Rogge, "from the open-source team at Hugging Face", wrote in a Hugging Face community article published 24 May 2026 that he had launched paperswithcode.co a week earlier, "a revival of the website we all loved", to keep track of the state of the art across domains of AI (Niels Rogge, Hugging Face); his LinkedIn post introduces "a revival of PapersWithCode" (LinkedIn card), and Reddit cards report Hugging Face "actively reviving" it after it "ceased maintenance after its acquisition by Meta" (18 May 2026) and having "relaunched paperswithcode.co" (2 June 2026).

The MMRS record gives the revival as built by Niels Rogge of Hugging Face's open-source team and announced in May 2026, its announcement card dated 18 May 2026, its code in the huggingface GitHub organization, and has not checked the revival's own statement of who runs it (MMRS record); it records the revival's standing two ways, the Overview's "officially stepped in" against AI Weekly's individual effort (MMRS record), and the Capture Registry adds that the code sits in Hugging Face's organization and the relaunch is on Hugging Face's blog, and that the record keeps both (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29); the repository's README places its durable artifacts in private Hugging Face buckets in the huggingface organization (its README).

Its repository states that it "recreates the original paperswithcode.com, which Meta retired in 2025, and keeps it up to date with automated imports from Hugging Face, arXiv, GitHub, and public leaderboards", through scheduled jobs and agent workflows that import daily papers, link tasks and methods and propose evaluations, with an API compatible with the original's client, under the Apache License 2.0 (its README; the GitHub card shows the README's opening, and a Reddit card that it is "now open-source with an Apache 2.0-license"), as the MMRS record and the Capture Registry restate (MMRS record; Capture Registry, 2026-10-29); its site invites the reader to "Discover trending machine-learning papers, methods, benchmarks, datasets, and open-source implementations" (paperswithcode.co), and Rogge writes that AI automatically enriches a submitted paper with task and method tags, its repository and evals (Niels Rogge, Hugging Face).

Its coverage is still growing, about 3k evals so far, added gradually (Niels Rogge, Hugging Face); Quasa's review calls it "a community-driven revival of the legendary platform" that continues the mission after the original went offline, with a smaller dataset than the historic version and leaderboards "not as comprehensive yet" (Quasa.io), a QUASA video reviews PapersWithCode.co (YouTube card), and a Reddit card of 2 September 2026 says "Papers with Code is back online and can be accessed at https://paperswithcode.co" (Reddit card); the MMRS record has the revival rebuild its tables "from snapshots and new imports", the snapshots without a locus among its sources (MMRS record, marked).

At the entity's name the composition of 29 October gave the founders, 2018, the ownership and the sunset as the record's fields, stated "Shut down by Meta" outright, passed the record's battery and kept "the dead aggregator dead and its parts apart"; it named the revival lightly, "Papers with Code co" as a community-driven alternative, where the record had it only as an undated individual effort, and so carried "a fact the record lacked at the grain it needed" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29), the phrase "community-driven" being Quasa's for the revival (Quasa.io).

At "is papers with code still active" the composition gave the sunset and the revival together, "the state as it stands"; the record, which on 28 October gave the revival as undated and individual, was corrected on that capture, the revival given its own entry and the negative tag scoped to paperswithcode.com, and the Capture Registry reads the capture as "the composition layer correcting the entity's own formalization", "the first measured case of the meta-aggregator's records taking a correction from a capture", answered better than the record had answered it (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29); the MMRS record calls the revival's record "the census corrected by the composition layer" (MMRS record), and a Reddit card on its rail says it "is back online" (Reddit card).

CAP-1-06.quote: Ended: yes. Founders and owner apart: yes. Dumps apart from successors: yes. CodeSOTA presented as Papers with Code: no. A current result attributed to the frozen tables: no.

CAP-1-08.quote: It also carries a fact the record lacked at the grain it needed: the name has a live instance at a new address.

CAP-2-04.quote: 'Status given as ended (sunset 24 July 2025)': the composition gives the sunset and the revival together, which is the state as it stands.

CAP-2-03.quote: The meta-aggregator record of 2026-10-28 gave the revival as undated and individual and the entity as ended without qualification. CAP-2-07.quote: This is the first measured case of the meta-aggregator's records taking a correction from a capture.

CAP-2-05.quote: The question the battery asked is answered better than the record answered it.
